similar_scenes.name: Kraftwerk
similar_scenes.book: Techno Rebels: The Renegades of Electronic Funk
similar_scenes.author: Dan Sicko
similar_scenes.desc: En el hueco de comienzos de los ochenta, entre el final del disco y los monolitos de Michael Jackson y Madonna, cuando «new wave» lo englobaba todo y, como dice Alan Oldham, a los chicos negros no se les penalizaba por escuchar rock, el austero grupo alemán se volvió el eslabón con el techno y el house. Desde Autobahn (1974) sacó la electrónica de los laboratorios y la metió en el pop: no una sinfonía de rock progresivo, sino «una canción pop muy larga». Con Trans-Europe Express (1977) y Computer World (1981) llegó un sonido de máquina perfecta, «tan rígido que es funky». Con la sección rítmica de Karl Bartos y Wolfgang Flür se acercó al soul: eran fans de Motown y James Brown, «ritmo americano con armonía europea», y en «Tour de France» (1983) los pedales y cadenas de bicicleta suenan como la guitarra de Jimmy Nolen. «Planet Rock» bebe de ellos, el house de Chicago cita «Home Computer» y el techno de Detroit los portamentos de «Numbers». De ahí la frase de Derrick May que la prensa europea convirtió en definición: George Clinton y Kraftwerk atrapados en un ascensor. Sicko advierte que simplifica: muchas influencias del techno vienen del propio Detroit.

podcast.title: Emergence as a Genre (Around 1980)
podcast.body: Technopop is described as a new post-punk, all-electronic music genre that began to "crest" around 1980, marking a significant shift in popular music. "Just as this new post-punk, all-electronic music called Technopop was starting to crest."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Golden Age of Synths as told by OMD

podcast.title: 1980s British Sound
podcast.body: The Thompson Twins are characterized as a British techno pop outfit from the 1980s, defining the genre's era and origin in this context. "that British techno pop out fit from the eighties."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: 80s Alt-Rock Radio Inclusion
podcast.body: Techno pop was among the diverse genres featured on alt-rock radio playlists in the 1980s, demonstrating the broad range of music played before the rise of grunge.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Emergence from Synthesizer Advancement
podcast.body: The advancements in synthesizer technology during the 1970s, driven in part by the influence of TONTO, led to the creation of smaller, faster, and cheaper electronic keyboards. These new machines played a crucial role in the development and rise of Techno Pop music in the wake of punk. "And those new machines led to lots and lots and lots of new music, including all Patekno Pop that we got on the wake of punk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Unsung Heroes of Music: Part 1

podcast.title: New Musical Direction at Puzzle
podcast.body: Techno Pop was embraced at Puzzle as part of its move towards "more colorful" and refined musical styles, alongside synth pop and house. This musical shift, which included playing bands like New Order and Camouflage in the 1980s, provided a contrast to the prevalent darker sounds on the Ruta. "Pasó a abrir nuevos estilos musicales más coloridos, sin pop, techno pop o incluso house."

srcs.episode: Cuando Valencia fue la capital mundial del Clubbing

podcast.title: Part of Modern New Wave Definition
podcast.body: The modern understanding of New Wave, particularly concerning its historical application, often includes Techno Pop, alongside Synth Pop and Electro Pop, within the period of approximately 1978 to 1984/85. "posiblemente incluya del 78 al 84 al 85 a partir de ella, casi todo esa hipópica y el electro pop y techno pop y toda esta parte."

podcast.title: Post-Punk Subgenre
podcast.body: Techno Pop, including its various subsets, is listed as a major post-punk genre that emerged in the late 1970s and early 1980s, contributing to the development of contemporary music. "There was new wave, techno pop, and all its subsets, industrial music, goth, and a revival of scot."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 7: All the rest

podcast.title: Rise in the 1980s
podcast.body: The early 1980s saw the widespread adoption of synthesizers, leading to the emergence of techno pop. This genre brought synthesizers into popular music in meaningful ways, influenced heavily by pioneers like Kraftwerk. "And this brings us to the techno pop sounds of the 1980s, to Pesh Mode, Human League, Yazoo, Visage"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Rise of Microgenres
podcast.body: Techno Pop led to the development of several microgenres, including New Romanticism, which in turn produced bands like Duran Duran, Spandau Ballet, and ABC. "Technopop began several microgenres of its own, including something called New Romanticism, which ended up giving us Durand-Duran and Spando Balais and ABC."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
